prompt: At the start of this lesson, who owns the tables customers and orders?
hint: Look at the Owner column of \dt.

choices.text: ana, who created them in lesson 4
choices.why: She did create them; lesson 12's layout.sql gave them to another role.

choices.text: app, which writes to them
choices.why: app writes rows and owns nothing, on purpose.

choices.text: shop_owner
choices.why: Right. A role nobody logs in as, so no password exists to drop them with.

choices.text: pg_database_owner, like the public schema
choices.why: pg_database_owner owns the schema; the tables belong to a real role.

prompt: In the start-up SQL, why does the CREATE VIEW come before layout.sql?
hint: What does layout.sql do to the view?

choices.text: layout.sql alters and grants on the view
choices.why: Right. ALTER VIEW ... OWNER TO and GRANT SELECT ON the view both need the view.

choices.text: Views must be created by a superuser
choices.why: Any role with CREATE on the schema and SELECT on what it reads can create one.

choices.text: Order is irrelevant in SQL files
choices.why: A script runs top to bottom; a statement on a missing object stops it.

choices.text: CREATE VIEW revokes CONNECT from PUBLIC as a side effect
choices.why: Creating a view touches no database privilege.

prompt: lesson 12 ran `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app`. shop_owner then creates refunds. What may app do with refunds?
hint: When did the GRANT run?

choices.text: Everything it may do on orders
choices.why: ON ALL TABLES reached the tables that existed then; refunds came later.

choices.text: Read it, since SELECT is inherited by new tables
choices.why: No privilege passes from one table to the next by itself.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. The insert was refused: the access list was empty, the owner alone.

choices.text: Everything, once the server is reloaded
choices.why: Grants are catalogue rows; a reload changes nothing about them.

prompt: Why is running `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` again after every migration the weakest of the three answers?
hint: Two failures: one of memory, one of reach.

choices.text: It locks every table while it runs
choices.why: That is not the argument the lesson made; the problem is what it remembers and what it reaches.

choices.text: It is refused for tables created by another role
choices.why: ana, a superuser, runs it with no refusal; the grants are recorded as the owner's.

choices.text: It does not exist in PostgreSQL 16
choices.why: It exists and ran in lesson 12.

choices.text: It relies on memory and grants too widely
choices.why: Right. It depends on memory, and it is too wide every time it runs.

prompt: After `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` is set, does refunds, created before it, get the grants?
hint: When is a default privilege applied?

choices.text: No; it needs a GRANT by hand
choices.why: Right. Two GRANT statements gave refunds what the defaults give new tables.

choices.text: Yes, at once
choices.why: \dp refunds was still empty right after the two statements.

choices.text: Yes, at the next VACUUM
choices.why: VACUUM has nothing to do with privileges.

choices.text: Yes, at the next login of app
choices.why: Privileges are on the table, not loaded with a session.

prompt: What does `FOR ROLE shop_owner` mean in `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE shop_owner IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting`?
hint: Whose new tables?

choices.text: Tables shop_owner creates
choices.why: Right. A default privilege belongs to the creating role.

choices.text: shop_owner receives the SELECT
choices.why: The grantee is after TO: reporting.

choices.text: Only shop_owner may run this statement
choices.why: ana, a superuser, ran it; FOR ROLE names whose objects it covers.

choices.text: Every table owned by shop_owner, old and new
choices.why: Old tables are untouched, and an owner change applies no defaults either.

prompt: ana creates coupons as herself, sees no grants, and runs `ALTER TABLE coupons OWNER TO shop_owner`. Can bruno read coupons now?
hint: When are defaults applied, and what does OWNER TO do?

choices.text: Yes, shop_owner's defaults follow the new owner
choices.why: Defaults are applied at creation, once; bruno was still refused.

choices.text: No: ownership moved and no default privilege was applied
choices.why: Right. Grant by hand, or recreate the table as shop_owner while it is empty.

choices.text: Yes, because reporting has SELECT on every table in public
choices.why: It has SELECT on the tables that existed or were created by shop_owner, and coupons is neither.

choices.text: No, because a table that changed owner is locked until a restart
choices.why: There is no such lock; the refusal is a missing privilege.

prompt: An administrator runs `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting` as herself. The deploy tool logs in as `deployer` and creates tables. What does reporting get on them?
hint: Without FOR ROLE, whose tables are meant?

choices.text: SELECT, because the default names the schema
choices.why: The schema narrows the default; it does not change whose tables it covers.

choices.text: SELECT, but only after deployer reconnects
choices.why: Reconnecting changes nothing about whose defaults apply.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. The defaults were recorded for the administrator's own tables, and deployer is somebody else.

choices.text: An error on every CREATE TABLE until FOR ROLE is added
choices.why: The tables are created without complaint, with no grants, which is why the trap is quiet.

prompt: A table with a serial column also needs `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT USAGE ON ___ TO app`.
hint: The plural object type that nextval reads.

prompt: Which single habit closes the creator trap for good?
hint: FOR ROLE names one role.

choices.text: Run ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES after every migration
choices.why: Defaults set after a table exists do nothing for it.

choices.text: Give reporting pg_read_all_data
choices.why: That reads email too and every future table, which is far wider than the layout wants.

choices.text: Run every migration as the role named in FOR ROLE, the owner role
choices.why: Right. Then every new table is created by the role whose defaults exist.

choices.text: Leave IN SCHEMA out
choices.why: That widens the schemas, not the creators.

prompt: Which psql command lists default privileges?
hint: One more d than the command for grants.

choices.text: \dp, which shows every grant
choices.why: It shows grants objects already have, never the defaults.

choices.text: \drg, with the role memberships
choices.why: That lists memberships and their options.

choices.text: \dn+, on the schema that holds them
choices.why: It shows the schema's own access list, not defaults for its future tables.

choices.text: \ddp
choices.why: Right. \dp shows what objects have; \ddp what new ones will get.

prompt: \ddp was empty on a fresh database. Does that mean a new function gives nothing to anybody?
hint: Are the built-in defaults rows?

choices.text: No: PUBLIC gets EXECUTE by a built-in default \ddp does not show
choices.why: Right. Revoking it made a row appear, without PUBLIC in it.

choices.text: Yes: an empty list means no grants
choices.why: Built-in defaults are not rows; the function row appeared only when somebody changed it.

choices.text: Yes, since PostgreSQL 15 removed EXECUTE from PUBLIC
choices.why: 15 removed CREATE on the public schema; EXECUTE on functions is still PUBLIC's.

choices.text: No: functions inherit the privileges of the schema
choices.why: Nothing is inherited from a schema; the default comes from the function's own built-in ACL.

prompt: A default `IN SCHEMA public` revokes SELECT from reporting, while a default with no schema grants it. What does a new table in public give reporting?
hint: A schema-level default only adds.

choices.text: Nothing, because the more specific default wins
choices.why: Per-schema defaults cannot take away what a global one gives.

choices.text: An error when the table is created
choices.why: Defaults never make a CREATE fail.

choices.text: SELECT
choices.why: Right. A default IN SCHEMA can only add to what applies everywhere.

choices.text: SELECT on the columns only
choices.why: Default privileges have no column form.

prompt: Order the steps to remove intern while keeping the table he made.
hint: Hand over first, clean up second, and in every database.
items: REASSIGN OWNED BY intern TO shop_owner, in shop
DROP OWNED BY intern, in shop
The same two statements, connected to ana
trap: Running DROP OWNED first drops the table instead of keeping it.

prompt: `DROP ROLE intern` in shop reports `1 object in database ana`. Why does it not say which object?
hint: Which catalogue can a session read?

choices.text: For security: other databases' names are secret
choices.why: It named the database; the object's name lives in that database's catalogue, which the session cannot read.

choices.text: A session sees only its own database's catalogue
choices.why: Right. The dependency is counted from a shared catalogue; the name is elsewhere.

choices.text: Because the object in ana is a temporary table
choices.why: It was an ordinary table, notes.

choices.text: Because ana is a superuser's database
choices.why: Ownership of the database plays no part in what DROP ROLE names.

prompt: What does `REASSIGN OWNED BY intern TO shop_owner` do?
hint: The table survives.

choices.text: Drops intern's objects
choices.why: That is DROP OWNED.

choices.text: Makes intern a member of shop_owner
choices.why: Membership is GRANT shop_owner TO intern; REASSIGN moves ownership.

choices.text: Moves intern's privileges, and only those, to shop_owner, in every database at once
choices.why: It moves ownership, not privileges, and acts on one database.

choices.text: Hands his objects here to shop_owner
choices.why: Right, and only in the current database.

prompt: You need a list of every privilege reporting holds in shop, quickly. Which statement gives it, and changes nothing?
hint: A refusal can be an inventory.

choices.text: `DROP ROLE reporting`, which fails and lists what depends on it
choices.why: Right, as long as the role does hold something; otherwise it succeeds.

choices.text: `\du reporting`
choices.why: \du shows attributes, not grants on objects.

choices.text: `REASSIGN OWNED BY reporting TO ana`
choices.why: That changes ownership, if there is any, and prints no list.

choices.text: `DROP OWNED BY reporting`
choices.why: That revokes everything it lists, which is the opposite of changing nothing.

prompt: intern had granted SELECT on reports.ideas to reporting. After REASSIGN OWNED to shop_owner, what happened to that grant?
hint: Look at \dp reports.ideas.

choices.text: It survived, with shop_owner as grantor
choices.why: Right. reporting still reads the table.

choices.text: It was dropped with intern
choices.why: reporting=r/shop_owner is still in the list.

choices.text: It became a default privilege
choices.why: Grants on an existing table stay grants on that table.

choices.text: It moved to intern's other table in ana
choices.why: Grants belong to one object and never move between databases.

prompt: auditor is a member of pg_read_all_data and nothing else. Can it log in to shop?
hint: Which door does pg_read_all_data stand in for?

choices.text: Yes, pg_read_all_data covers every privilege a reader needs
choices.why: It covers tables and schemas. has_database_privilege said f for CONNECT.

choices.text: Yes, predefined roles skip pg_hba.conf
choices.why: Nothing skips pg_hba.conf, and the database door is a privilege, not a pg_hba.conf line.

choices.text: No: CONNECT on shop is not part of it
choices.why: Right. shop gives CONNECT only to app and reporting.

choices.text: No, because predefined roles cannot be granted to a LOGIN role
choices.why: auditor was created LOGIN IN ROLE pg_read_all_data without complaint.

prompt: Without pg_monitor, what does bruno see in the query column for app's session in pg_stat_activity?
hint: The row is there, its contents are not.

choices.text: `<insufficient privilege>`
choices.why: Right. The session's existence is visible; what it does is not.

choices.text: Nothing: the row is absent
choices.why: The row appeared, with the pid and the user.

choices.text: SELECT pg_sleep(60), as for anyone
choices.why: That needed pg_monitor, granted afterwards.

choices.text: An error: permission denied for view pg_stat_activity
choices.why: The view is readable by everybody; it hides columns instead.

prompt: Match each predefined role to who it is for.
hint: One of them is a superuser by another name.

pairs.right: A backup tool or an auditor
An on-call engineer stopping runaway queries
Almost nobody: it runs programs on the server

prompt: An on-call engineer has pg_signal_backend. A superuser's maintenance session is blocking everybody. Can the engineer terminate it?
hint: What is the role safe against?

choices.text: Yes: pg_signal_backend terminates any session
choices.why: It reaches sessions of roles that are not superusers, and stops there.

choices.text: Yes, with pg_monitor as well
choices.why: pg_monitor shows queries; it adds no power to terminate.

choices.text: Only by cancelling the query, not by terminating the session
choices.why: Cancelling a superuser's query is refused in the same way.

choices.text: No: a superuser's session is out of its reach
choices.why: Right, which is what makes the role safe to hand out; this one needs a superuser.

prompt: A new analytics table is created every month by the migration role shop_owner, and reporting must read each one on the day it appears. What do you set, once?
hint: Whose tables, which schema, which grantee.

choices.text: `GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO reporting`
choices.why: That covers the tables of today and none of next month's.

choices.text: `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting`, run as ana
choices.why: Without FOR ROLE it covers ana's tables, and the migrations create shop_owner's.

choices.text: `GRANT pg_read_all_data TO reporting`
choices.why: It works and gives email and everything else too, which the layout refuses.

choices.text: `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE shop_owner IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting`
choices.why: Right. Every table shop_owner creates there arrives readable.

prompt: An employee who owns tables in three databases leaves. `DROP ROLE` fails in the first database with `2 objects in database sales`. What is the procedure?
hint: REASSIGN and DROP OWNED act on one database.

choices.text: Run DROP ROLE with CASCADE
choices.why: DROP ROLE has no CASCADE; the server makes you decide object by object.

choices.text: DROP OWNED in the first database only; it reaches the others
choices.why: It acts on the current database; the lesson needed a second connection to ana.

choices.text: ALTER ROLE ... NOLOGIN, since a role that owns things is never dropped
choices.why: NOLOGIN is a fine first step, but the role can be dropped once its objects are handed over.

choices.text: Hand over and clean up per database, then drop
choices.why: Right. The DETAIL of each failed DROP ROLE lists the databases left to visit.

prompt: How many predefined `pg_` roles did the query list on PostgreSQL 16?
hint: Count the rows.
